title: God heals the called: new habitual holiness
source_text: VI. Verum Deus in iis, quos misericorditer per fidem ad se vocat, tantis malis me-detur. Ex mente siquidem tenebras per peccatum inductas dispellit, illamque coelesti quadam & divina luce collustrat. Pravam voluntatem corrigit, & cor durum emollit, bonique amore accendit & inflammat. Denique perturbatos & inordinatos affectus & appetitus componit, & cogit in ordinem, ipsamque rebellem concupiscentiam do-minio spoliat, & quasi sub jugum mittit. Ex quibus omnibus exurgit sanctitas & justitia illa nova, quam, verbo Dei duce, in fidelibus ultro agnoscimus, quaeque, ut satis ex dictis apparet, in solis quibusdam bonis operibus non consistit, sed potissimum in interna quadam & permanenti gratia, quae per modum habitus animam afficit & ex-ornat.
pass_a_gloss: But God heals such great evils in those whom he mercifully calls to himself by faith. From the mind he dispels the darkness introduced by sin and illuminates it with a certain heavenly and divine light. He corrects the depraved will and softens the hard heart, kindling and inflaming it with love of the good. Finally he composes disordered affections and appetites and brings them into order, strips rebellious concupiscence of its dominion, and as it were puts it under the yoke. From all these arises that new holiness and righteousness which, with the Word of God as guide, we freely acknowledge in believers, and which, as is clear enough from what has been said, does not consist in certain good works alone, but chiefly in a certain internal and permanent grace which affects and adorns the soul after the manner of a habit.
pass_b_english: In the mercifully called, God dispels mental darkness, softens the hard heart, orders disordered appetites.
New holiness rises chiefly as an internal lasting habitual grace, not merely isolated good works.
